prompt:
Find real, published measurements of how much battery life a typical Bluetooth LE smart home sensor (e.g. Zigbee or BLE door/temperature sensors) actually achieves in the field, as opposed to manufacturer claims. Cite the sources and quote the figures.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on my search, I found several real-world measurements for Zigbee sensor battery life. However, I could not find any published field measurements specifically for **Bluetooth LE (BLE)** smart home sensors. The search results were exclusively focused on Zigbee and Z-Wave technologies.

Here are the relevant findings for Zigbee sensors, which were the only type of field measurements I could locate:

SOURCE: https://www.thesmarthomebook.com/2020/12/04/xiaomi-aqara-2-year-review/ | QUOTE: "Motion sensor 1 (RTCGQ01LM) : sits on the landing and of an evening, turns on nightlights for a period of time and then if no further motion detected after a couple of minutes, turns the lights back off... Battery life: 36%" | CLAIM: A frequently used Xiaomi motion sensor had 36% battery remaining after two years of use.
SOURCE: https://www.thesmarthomebook.com/2020/12/04/xiaomi-aqara-2-year-review/ | QUOTE: "Motion sensor 2 (RTCGQ01LM): sits in a cupboard and turns on additional lighting when the cupboard doors are open, and again, if no further motion detected turns the lights back off. Used rarely, couple of times a week if that. Battery life: 100%" | CLAIM: An infrequently used Xiaomi motion sensor had 100% battery remaining after two years of use.
SOURCE: https://www.thesmarthomebook.com/2020/12/04/xiaomi-aqara-2-year-review/ | QUOTE: "Office- Battery life: 37%" | CLAIM: A frequently used Xiaomi temperature/humidity/pressure sensor had 37% battery remaining after two years of use.
SOURCE: https://asidehouse.com/gizmo/a-year-with-aqara-motion-sensors-dotted-round-the-house/ | QUOTE: "The two bathroom sensors, which trigger dozens of times a day given how often that space is used, are the closest to needing a swap at the twelve-month mark, currently reporting under 20% in the app." | CLAIM: Heavily used Aqara motion sensors were nearing end of battery life (~20% remaining) after one year.
SOURCE: https://asidehouse.com/gizmo/a-year-with-aqara-motion-sensors-dotted-round-the-house/ | QUOTE: "The garage sensor, triggered only a handful of times a week, still shows over 70% remaining." | CLAIM: An infrequently used Aqara motion sensor had over 70% battery remaining after one year.
SOURCE: https://johal.in/benchmark-zigbee-30-vs-z-wave-vs-wi-fi-smart | QUOTE: "| 30 seconds | 14.3 | 18.2 | 4.3 |" | CLAIM: In a controlled benchmark test, a Zigbee 3.0 contact sensor reporting every 30 seconds achieved a battery life of 14.3 months.
SOURCE: https://johal.in/benchmark-zigbee-30-vs-z-wave-vs-wi-fi-smart | QUOTE: "| 60 seconds | 22.7 | 28.5 | 7.1 |" | CLAIM: In a controlled benchmark test, a Zigbee 3.0 contact sensor reporting every 60 seconds achieved a battery life of 22.7 months.
SOURCE: https://johal.in/benchmark-zigbee-30-vs-z-wave-vs-wi-fi-smart | QUOTE: "Zigbee 3.0 battery life dropped by 18% (14.3 to 11.7 months) due to retransmissions" | CLAIM: In a real-world test with Wi-Fi interference, the battery life of a Zigbee sensor reporting every 30 seconds dropped to 11.7 months.

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Real, published measurements of battery life for a typical Bluetooth LE (BLE) smart home sensor (e.g., door/temperature sensors) achieved in the field.
